2. RELATED WORK

To our knowledge, the chain P was first studied by Diaconis and Saloff-Coste [6], who used a comparison with another chain on I studied by Hildebrand [8] to get an upper bound of O(n?) on the relaxation time (the inverse of the spectral gap), implying an upper bound of O (nt) on the l'-mixing time. Then the results of Kassabov [9] on the Kazhdan constant yield an upper bound of O(n?) on the l'-mixing time, which was the best known upper bound for total variation mixing as well. As for the lower bound, a simple counting argument shows that the total-variation mixing time can be lower bounded by I (which is actually an estimate of the diameter of the underlying graph, see Andrén et al.
